**Testing many hypotheses gives chance more opportunities to look significant.** With 20 independent true nulls each tested at 0.05, the probability of at least one false rejection is $1-0.95^{20}\approx64\%$. Independence is needed for that exact calculation, but the general multiplicity problem does not disappear when metrics are correlated. [1](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/stats.html)

**Bonferroni protects against any false discovery in the family.** Test each of m hypotheses at alpha/m. The union bound controls family-wise error without requiring independence, though the method can be conservative, particularly with correlated tests.

**Benjamini–Hochberg targets a different error quantity.** Sort p-values and compare the kth to $k\alpha/m$ under the procedure's assumptions. It controls the expected fraction of false discoveries among discoveries rather than the probability of any false discovery. This can be more appropriate for exploratory screening, where some false leads are tolerable.

Neither method means every declared result has a known individual probability of being false. Also, BH's standard guarantees have dependence conditions; arbitrary selection and repeated peeking are not automatically covered.

Define the testing family and primary outcome before inspecting results. A team that tests fifty metrics but reports only the best one has not avoided multiplicity by showing one chart. Use effect sizes and uncertainty alongside corrected decisions, and reserve independent confirmation for important exploratory findings.

**Technical details and references.**

With 20 independent true null tests at 0.05, the chance of at least one false rejection is $1-0.95^{20}\approx64.2\%$. Bonferroni tests each of $m$ hypotheses at $\alpha/m$, controlling family-wise error even without independence. [1](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/stats.html)

Benjamini–Hochberg sorts p-values and finds the largest $k$ satisfying $p_{(k)}\le kq/m$, then rejects through $k$. Under its required dependence conditions, it controls expected false-discovery proportion rather than probability of any false discovery.

Define the family before inspecting results. Correlated metrics, exploratory slices, and selective reporting complicate guarantees; use appropriate dependence-robust methods when necessary. Pick control according to decision cost: a safety-critical confirmatory claim may require stronger error protection than an exploratory discovery screen.
